Module-1 Explain: (i) Stress (ii) Strain (iii) Modulus of Elasticity (06 Marks) Define four elastic constraints. (08 Marks) Determine the stresses in various segments of circular bar shown in the Fig.Q1(c). Also compute the total elongation taking Young’s modulus E = 195 GPa. Fig.Q1(c) (06 Marks) OR Derive an expression for the deformation of a rectangular tapering bar of uniform thickness subjected to an axial force. (10 Marks) A steel tube of 80 mm outer diameter and 10 mm thick is filled into a copper tube of 30 mm inner diameter and 10 mm thick. They are connected rigidly at the ends and subjected to an axial compression of 300 kN load. If length of bar is 600 mm, find the stresses in each material. Take E s = 200 GPa and E cu = 120 GPa. (05 Marks) A steel rod of 3 cm diameter and 5 m long is connected to two grips and the rod is maintained at temperature of 95  C. Determine the stresses and pull exerted when temperature falls below 30  C if: (i) The ends are not yielding (ii) The ends yields by 0.12 cm Take E = 2  10 5 MN/m 2 and  = 12  10 -6 /  C. (05 Marks) Module-2 Explain maximum shear stress theory of failure. (08 Marks) A cast iron pipe 200 mm internal diameter and 50 mm metal thickness carries water under a pressure of 5 N/mm 2 . Calculate the maximum and minimum intensities of circumferential stresses and sketch the distribution of circumferential stress intensity and intensity of radial pressure across the cross section. (12 Marks) OR Differentiate between thick and thin cylinders. (02 Marks) For thin cylinder, derive the equations for circumferential stress and longitudinal stress. (08 Marks) Important Note : 1.
